title: Speed, Cost and Model Routing
summary: Reflex providers, D1 shadow, and honest cost

lessons.title: Reflex providers
lessons.body: Nerve supports pluggable Reflex providers: Jev (remote), OpenJev, Laya, and Liquid D1 (local HTTP service, LOCAL_ONLY).

lessons.title: Shadow first
lessons.body: New providers start as async shadow comparators: the authoritative answer is unchanged; paired records measure agreement.

lessons.title: Honest cost
lessons.body: Billed savings count only APPLY-mode plans that actually reach model-visible context.

lab.goal: Enable a local D1 endpoint in shadow mode and read the paired-record metrics.
steps: Point reflex_backend at a loopback D1 service (see docs/LOCAL_BACKEND_GUIDE.md).
Enable shadow_testing for one profile only.
Read reflex metrics after a few turns; note paired vs agreement counts.
lab.expect: You can explain why shadow plans are not billed savings.

task.intro: Answer the scenario questions; the engine verifies them deterministically in a disposable fixture. Your answers are never executed as commands.

questions.q: In shadow mode, is the paired comparison billed as a decision? (yes/no)
questions.why: Shadow comparisons are observations, not billed decision savings.

questions.q: What provenance marks a local D1 answer?
Does an HTTP health check prove inference works? (yes/no)
questions.why: Health is not a typed inference validation.

executable.task: Route economics: choose routes per workload and compute the total from the supplied table. The engine re-executes your arithmetic.

check.question: Q: Which mode must a profile be in for D1 answers to be authoritative?

troubleshooting: LOCAL_ONLY is enforced: loopback HTTPS endpoints only, no model weights in the plugin.
Promotion to primary requires separate acceptance - it is never implicit.
